exact_missing_items: The base `GraphNode` struct still preserves stale fields as if they were core model state:
The event-family layer is still one of the last upstream carriers of stale execution semantics.

The final pass confirms the broader second sweep reached diminishing returns only after the sixth model: the remaining signal is mostly exact structural canon breakage, stale owner-routing, and field/command/schema mismatches rather than broad new conceptual seams.
The middle of the file still preserves stale execution ontology:
The owner docs now have a split between modern canonical field names and stale canonical scope language.
The same consumer docs now rely on canonical blocked/scheduler/remediation lineage in one section and legacy tier-event push streams in another.
The unresolved shape is still the same: missing owner anchors, skeletal consumer carry-through, and exact stale contradictory survivors.
This is no longer only “storage is stale in places.” The document now carries multiple overlapping canonicality layers from different rewrite stages.

This pass keeps all `8` blocker families open, but it sharpens the unresolved set so follow-on audit work can target exact missing anchors and stale survivors instead of re-auditing already transferred fields.
This seam is owner-level, not consumer-level. Fixing `Orchestrator_Page.md` or `FinalGUISpec.md` first would still leave stale routing at the top of the precedence stack.
